verdicts.reason: A puts the body copy directly on top of the teal circle (a collision), and the can floats beside an empty circle instead of sitting in it, with GLACIER placed under the headline. B avoids the text collision, but the circle is still an empty orphan detached from the can, and the body copy is cut off from its headline and stranded at the far right edge.

A is the same layout as pair 1 A: body text sits on the circle, the can floats free of its backdrop, and the headline, brand and buttons are crowded into the right half. B has no collisions, but the circle is an empty disc, the can and body copy are pushed into a separate cluster on the right with dead space between, and the badge reads 'BACK BYDEMAND' (missing space).

A groups the copy sensibly, but the body line under GLACIER is shrunk to an illegible size, the circle is empty, and the can is stranded at the right after a large dead gap. B keeps the body copy readable, but it is detached at the far right, the circle is empty next to the can, and GLACIER is subordinated below the headline.

Both overlay the body copy on the teal circle (collision) and separate the can from its circle. A's CTA text is squeezed ('FindItNearYou') and leaves a large empty gap before the can. B has a stronger, larger headline and better use of width, but still has the collision and a tiny, isolated can.
